description: "The challenge of making useful predictions when little data or interaction history is available."
term: "Cold Start"

difficulty: "Intermediate"

## Simple explanation

The cold-start problem occurs when a system has too little information
about a new user, item, or environment to make reliable personalized
predictions.

## Technical explanation

In recommender systems, cold start commonly refers to new users with no
interaction history, new items with few interactions, or a new system with
limited data overall. Strategies include onboarding questions, content
features, popularity priors, metadata, and exploration.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

A recommender that depends only on historical interactions may fail for
new users or products. Cold-start handling affects user experience,
coverage, fairness, and the ability to surface new items.

## How it works

The system combines available signals with fallback methods. For a new
item, metadata or content embeddings may support recommendations before
interactions accumulate. For a new user, explicit preferences or
contextual signals can provide an initial estimate. The system can update
personalization as feedback arrives.

## Practical example

A book recommender can use genre and description embeddings to suggest a
newly added book before it has ratings, then incorporate user interactions
as they become available.

## Common misconceptions

- Cold start is not the same as concept drift or a sudden model failure.
- Popularity-based recommendations can provide a fallback but may reduce
  discovery or reinforce existing exposure patterns.
- More user data does not automatically remove all recommendation bias.
